newsitem.title: USA: Reader's Digest revamps Brazilian version.
newsitem.headline: Reader's Digest revamps Brazilian version.

text.p: Reader's Digest Association Inc said Wednesday it had launched a revitalized Brazilian-language edition of Selecoes do Reader's Digest in a bid to build its subscription base dramatically over the next five years.
The publisher said that a marketing blitz had increased audited circulation of Selecoes do Reader's Digest to 350,000 from 50,000 in the past year.

William H. Willis, President of Reader's Digest Pacific, said in a statement, "Of Brazil's 20 million households, we project that we will reach over one million of them, or five percent, in the next five years."

Willis said expansion in Brazil would be in keeping with the company's strategy to grow business by expanding into new and growing markets and finding new channels for the distribution of Reader's Digest products.
The company said Selecoes do Reader's Digest was one of its first international editions when it was launched in 1942.
The publisher has been battling weakness in many of its markets and announced last month that it sees earnings for the third quarter and the fiscal year below market expectations.
